title: Interview Flashcards & Exam Questions: Endpoint Security

flashcards.question: What is the key functional difference between EPP and EDR?
flashcards.answer: EPP (Endpoint Protection Platform) focuses on PREVENTING file-based and known malware using signatures, heuristics, and device control before execution. EDR (Endpoint Detection & Response) focuses on CONTINUOUS DETECTING and INVESTIGATING suspicious activity via behavioral analysis, process tree reconstruction, and automated host isolation after execution.

flashcards.question: Why is signature-only traditional antivirus insufficient against modern attacks?
flashcards.answer: Traditional AV relies on known file hashes/signatures. Modern attacks use fileless malware (running entirely in memory via PowerShell or WMI), zero-day exploits, and encrypted payloads that lack existing signatures.

flashcards.question: What is Agent Tamper Protection and why is it mandatory?
flashcards.answer: Tamper Protection prevents malicious processes or rogue local administrators from stopping the EDR agent service, modifying registry keys, or disabling real-time scanning during an active breach.

flashcards.question: Explain XDR (Extended Detection and Response) and how it expands on EDR.
flashcards.answer: EDR collects telemetry strictly from endpoints. XDR correlates telemetry across multiple security layers — endpoints, network firewalls, cloud workloads, email gateways, and identity providers (Azure AD) — to trace full multi-stage attack chains.
